en: The Sūtra on the Exposition of the Analysis of Dependent Origination and Other Topics.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great saṅgha of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks.
There, the Blessed One addressed them: "Monks, I shall teach you the beginning of dependent origination and its analysis.
Listen to that."
Pay close and careful attention; I shall speak:
what is the beginning of dependent origination?
Namely, when this exists, that comes to be.
With the arising of this, that arises;
namely, conditioned by ignorance are the formative forces (saṃskāra),
and conditioned by the formative forces is consciousness (vijñāna).
Conditioned by consciousness is name-and-form;
conditioned by name-and-form are the six sense bases;
conditioned by the six sense bases is contact.
Conditioned by contact is feeling;
conditioned by feeling is craving;
conditioned by craving is grasping.
With clinging as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises;
and with birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, depression, and despair come into being.
In this way, there is the origination of this entire great mass of suffering;
this is called the beginning of dependent origination.
What is the analysis?
Regarding the statement "conditioned by ignorance are the formative forces," what is ignorance?
It is the lack of knowledge concerning the past.
Ignorance regarding the future, ignorance regarding both the past and the future,
and ignorance regarding the internal.
knowledge of the external, knowledge of both the internal and the external,
and knowledge of skillfulness;
Ignorance regarding maturation, ignorance regarding the maturation of karma,
and ignorance regarding the Buddha.
ignorance regarding the Dharma,
ignorance regarding the Saṅgha, and ignorance regarding suffering;
ignorance regarding the origin, ignorance regarding cessation, and ignorance regarding the path;
Ignorance regarding causes;
ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from causes;

ignorance regarding wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, blameworthy and blameless phenomena, those to be cultivated and those not to be cultivated, inferior and superior phenomena, dark and bright phenomena, and phenomena that are their counterparts produced through dependent origination.
Or again, it is the thorough penetration of the six bases of contact as they truly are;
that which here and there is the lack of knowledge regarding things as they truly are.
non-seeing, non-realization,
darkness;
Delusion, the darkness of ignorance— this is called ignorance (avidyā).
What are the formations conditioned by ignorance?
There are three types of formations: bodily formations, vocal formations, and mental formations.
"Consciousness has formations as its condition. What is consciousness?
It is the six groups of consciousness: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness.
Regarding the statement "name-and-form has consciousness as its condition," what is name?
It is the four formless aggregates.
Which four?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
What is form?
Whatever is form—

All that consists of the four great elements and that which is derived from the four great elements— this is "name"; when these two are condensed together into a single unity, it is called "name-and-form" (nāmarūpa).
"Conditioned by name-and-form are the six sense bases. What are the six sense bases?
They are the six internal sense bases:
the internal eye base, and the internal ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind bases.
"Contact has the six sense bases as its condition. What is contact?
It is the six groups of contact:
visual contact, and auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental contact.
"Feeling has contact as its condition. What is feeling?
There are three feelings.
Pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant.
"With feeling as condition, craving arises. What is craving?
There are three types of craving:
craving for sensual pleasures, craving for form, and craving for the formless.
"Appropriation has craving as its condition. What is appropriation?
There are four types of appropriation:
appropriation of sensual desire, appropriation of views, appropriation of rules and observances, and appropriation of the doctrine of self.
"Existence has grasping as its condition. What is existence?
There are three existences:
existence in the realm of desire, existence in the realm of form, and existence in the formless realm.
"Birth has existence as its condition. What is birth?

It is the birth, the being born, the descent, the manifestation, the appearance, the acquisition of the aggregates, the acquisition of the elements, the acquisition of the sense bases, and the full development of the aggregates for this or that being within this or that class of beings.
The manifestation of the life-faculty.
"Old age and death have birth as their condition. What is old age?

It is that which consists of baldness, graying hair, an abundance of wrinkles, decrepitude, stooping, being bent like a curved roof-beam, the body being covered with dark spots, the body being labored by shortness of breath, the body leaning forward, the need for support by a staff, slowness, and dullness.
Decline, diminution, the maturation of the faculties, the breaking down of conditioned phenomena, their becoming ancient, and their becoming worn out—
this is called old age.
What is death?

It is the passing away, the falling away, the dissolution, the disappearance from each respective class of beings; it is the exhaustion of the life-span, the exhaustion of heat, the cessation of the life-faculty, the casting off of the aggregates, death, and the completion of one's time.
This is called death;
and this death, together with prior aging— these two, when condensed into a single unity, are called "aging-and-death."
This is called the analysis of dependent origination.
That which was said to you— "I shall teach you the beginning of dependent origination" and "its analysis"—
that has now been explained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One;
with uplifted minds, those monks rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The Sūtra on the Exposition of the Analysis of Dependent Origination and so forth is completed.
